# The diagnostic wordings that no surviving case exercises (WP19 G2.4).
#
# Every code here is a message the compiler can print and nothing checks the
# words of. Today they are proved by stage0 and stage1 agreeing; after R6 that
# comparison is gone and they would be proved by nothing, so this file is a
# work list rather than a list of exemptions.
#
# GENERATED by scripts/check-diagnostic-coverage.mjs --update, except for the
# notes: everything after `##` on a line is written by hand and kept across a
# regeneration. A note says *why* nothing reaches the rule, and it is what
# separates the two kinds of entry here — a case nobody has written yet, and a
# rule no program can reach because another one fires first.
#
# The check is a ratchet: a code that leaves this file may not come back, and a
# code that is not here and not covered fails the run. Write a `reject_*`
# case, run the script with --update, and the line disappears.
#
# 19 live codes, measured against every `reject_*` case, the
# `tests/link/` negatives, the driver command lines and the programs that warn.
# Retired and shadowed rules are not here and never will be: no message
# contains their words, or a longer fragment always wins, so no case can reach
# them either way.

NL2011  #  are not supported  ## Phase 0 refuses the type parameters first (NL1045, `reject_generic_class`), so the checker's own message for a generic class or interface is never reached.
NL2019  #  needs a type annotation  ## shadowed through an interpolation: every message with these words puts a name in backticks in front of them, so the longer "` needs a type annotation" matches first. The static shadow check in the generator cannot see it, because the backtick comes from the interpolation.
NL2031  # : unsupported modifier `  ## the same shape as NL2019: `${what}` always ends in a backtick, so "`: unsupported modifier `" wins (`reject_cls_field_declare` pins those words).
NL2072  # ` is a constant imported from `  ## needs the name recorded as used-as-a-type before the import binds; every arrangement tried resolves the annotation to an unknown type first and reports that instead.
NL2073  # ` is a function imported from `  ## as NL2072, for an imported function.
NL2075  # ` is already declared as a function  ## structs are declared before functions, so the clash is always reported the other way round, as NL2074 (`reject_cls_name_is_function`).
NL2109  # ` when checking a single module  ## the single-module checking path the dump entry points use; the CLI always loads the program whole, so no command line reaches it.
NL2125  # `declare function` is not supported yet  ## the missing body is checked first, so `declare function f(): number;` is NL2204 (`reject_fn_declare`).
NL2133  # `for await` is not supported  ## `for await` needs an `async` function, which Phase 0 refuses first (NL1015).
NL2173  # async functions are not supported  ## Phase 0 refuses `async` first (NL1015, `reject_async_function`).
NL2174  # async methods are not supported  ## as NL2173, for a method.
NL2205  # Generators are not supported  ## Phase 0 refuses generators first (NL1044, `reject_generator`).
NL2207  # Generic functions are not supported  ## Phase 0 refuses type parameters first (NL1045).
NL2208  # Generic methods are not supported  ## as NL2207, for a method.
NL2211  # Import must name the functions it imports  ## an import clause with neither a name nor named bindings cannot be written: the grammar always gives one or the other.
NL2216  # internal: array method on non-array  ## an internal invariant. Reaching it would be a compiler bug rather than a program.
NL2217  # Labelled `break` is not supported  ## Phase 0 refuses labeled statements first (NL1046).
NL2218  # Labelled `continue` is not supported  ## as NL2217, for `continue`.
NL2252  # Unsupported `new   ## dead: `newCheckers["*"]` is always present, so the lookup never falls through to this message.
